names.official: Personal income tax, share of the State

taxes.base: Wages, self-employment and other income of residents, and Latvian-source income of non-residents.

rate.headline: 20% · 23% · 31% in 2024; 25.5% · 33% from 2025
details: 2024: 20% up to EUR 20,004 a year, 23% from EUR 20,004 to 78,100, 31% above.
From 2025 there are two rates: 25.5% up to EUR 105,300 and 33% above (Ministry of Finance table).

instruments.explanation: The National Tax List gives the total tax of EUR 2,870 million; Eurostat’s accounts place EUR 2,167 million of it with local governments and the rest with the State. This row is the State’s part, the next the municipalities’.
exceptions: The Ministry’s table also shows a minimum not subject to tax and a solidarity tax of 25% above the ceiling of the social contributions.

names.official: Corporate income tax

taxes.base: Profit that a company distributes (dividends, deemed distributions) and certain non-business expenses, not the profit it keeps.

rate.headline: 20% of the gross amount (20/80 of the net)
details: The standard rate; from 1 January 2026 an alternative 15% rate on dividends, with 6% personal income tax on them, is available to companies owned only by individuals (Ministry of Finance).

instruments.explanation: Like Estonia, Latvia taxes company profit when it is distributed, not when it is earned. Revenue rose 46% in 2024.

names.official: Mandatory state social insurance contributions, employers’ part
names.native: Darba devēju valsts sociālās apdrošināšanas obligātās iemaksas

taxes.base: Gross pay, up to an annual ceiling (EUR 78,100 in 2024, EUR 105,300 from 2025).

rate.headline: 23.59% of gross pay
details: Total rate 34.09% in 2024, 2025 and 2026: employer 23.59%, employee 10.5% (Ministry of Finance table).

instruments.explanation: The biggest social payment. The National Tax List splits it into pension (EUR 2,117 million) and non-pension (EUR 907 million) contributions.

names.official: Mandatory state social insurance contributions, employees’ part
names.native: Darba ņēmēju valsts sociālās apdrošināšanas obligātās iemaksas

taxes.base: Gross pay, up to the same annual ceiling.

rate.headline: 10.5% of gross pay
details: Employee rate 10.5% in 2024 to 2026 (Ministry of Finance table).

instruments.explanation: Pays for pensions, sickness, maternity, unemployment and other social insurance benefits.

names.official: Contributions of the self-employed and voluntary contributions

taxes.base: The income of self-employed people; voluntary contributions of persons who insure themselves.
taxes.payer: Self-employed people and voluntary insured persons.

rate.headline: Set by the Law on State Social Insurance
details: The National Tax List separates EUR 62.3 million of compulsory contributions of the self-employed from EUR 0.3 million of voluntary ones.

instruments.explanation: The remaining part of the households’ actual social contributions.

names.official: Value added tax

taxes.base: Goods and services supplied in Latvia, intra-EU acquisitions and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and claim input credits.

rate.headline: 21% standard; 12% and 5% reduced
details: The Ministry of Finance page names the 12% and 5% reduced rates (books and press 5%; a pilot 12% on certain foods from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027).

instruments.explanation: The largest tax by far.

names.official: Customs duties

taxes.base: Goods imported from outside the EU, by the Common Customs Tariff.

rate.headline: EU Common Customs Tariff
details: An EU own resource; Eurostat records it under the EU institutions (sector S.212: EUR 63 million).

instruments.explanation: Collected by the State Revenue Service for the EU budget.

names.official: Excise duty on oil products

taxes.base: Petrol, diesel, heating oil and other oil products, by quantity.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on at the pump.

rate.headline: Per 1,000 litres or per tonne
details: The rates are fixed in the Law on Excise Duties.

instruments.explanation: The biggest excise.

names.official: Excise duty on tobacco

taxes.base: Cigarettes, cigars and other tobacco products.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Fixed by the Law on Excise Duties

instruments.explanation: The second largest excise.

names.official: Excise duty on alcohol and on beer

taxes.base: Spirits, wine, intermediate products, fermented drinks and beer, by volume or pure alcohol.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per 100 litres, rising each 1 March
details: On 1 March 2026 the rate for wine rose from EUR 134 to EUR 148 per 100 litres and for other alcoholic drinks from EUR 1,955 to EUR 2,084 per 100 litres of absolute alcohol; further steps are fixed for 2027 and 2028 (Ministry of Finance).

instruments.explanation: The National Tax List shows alcohol (EUR 210.5 million) and beer (EUR 53.9 million) as separate lines.

names.official: Excise duty on natural gas, electricity and other excise goods; excise on imports
names.native: Akcīzes nodoklis dabasgāzei, elektroenerģijai un pārējām precēm

taxes.base: Natural gas, electricity and the other excise goods, plus excise collected on imports released for free circulation.

rate.headline: Fixed by the Law on Excise Duties
details: EUR 41.1 million other excise goods, 13.2 million natural gas, 4.9 million electricity and 1.5 million excise on imports in 2024.

instruments.explanation: Smaller lines of the excise family.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LV, D214A C04, C06, C07 and D2122C C01

names.official: Lottery and gambling tax and state duties on lotteries and gambling
names.native: Loteriju un azartspēļu nodoklis un valsts nodevas

taxes.base: Gambling operators’ takings and the organising of lotteries.

rate.headline: Set by the Gambling and Lotteries Law
details: EUR 54.4 million lottery and gambling tax, EUR 3.4 million state duty on lotteries and gambling and EUR 0.4 million duty on lotteries of goods and services in 2024. The Ministry of Finance lists changes to the gambling tax from 2026.

instruments.explanation: Three lines in the National Tax List that tax the same activity.

names.official: Vehicle operation tax (legal and natural persons) and company car tax
names.native: Transportlīdzekļa ekspluatācijas nodoklis; uzņēmumu vieglo transportlīdzekļu nodoklis

taxes.base: Registered road vehicles; passenger cars owned by companies.

rate.headline: By engine, mass and emissions
details: EUR 71.4 million came from vehicles registered to natural persons, EUR 31.0 million from those registered to legal persons and EUR 28.5 million from the company car tax in 2024. The Ministry of Finance lists changes to the vehicle operation tax from 2026.

instruments.explanation: An annual tax on owning a vehicle.

names.official: Natural resources tax

taxes.base: Use of natural resources, pollution and waste disposal.

rate.headline: Set by the Natural Resources Tax Law
details: Eurostat’s accounts place EUR 17 million of the permit and natural-resource revenue with local government.

instruments.explanation: An environmental tax. The sale of emission permits (EUR 90.8 million) is not counted.

names.official: Security reserve service fee

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: the fee for the service of keeping security reserves (of oil products).

rate.headline: Not given in the list
details: The list shows a "state duty for keeping oil products’ security reserves" of EUR 73.6 million in 2023 and the fee above in 2024.

instruments.explanation: A compulsory charge that the statistician books as a tax on products.

names.official: Contributions to the Deposit Guarantee Fund and the mortgage borrower protection duty
names.native: Iemaksas noguldījumu garantiju fondā; hipotekārā kredīta ņēmēju aizsardzības nodeva

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List (contributions to the Deposit Guarantee Fund; a duty described as protecting mortgage borrowers); the list gives no further detail.

rate.headline: Set by law
details: EUR 97.5 million mortgage borrower protection duty (a new line in 2024), EUR 22.3 million Deposit Guarantee Fund; the Single Resolution Fund line is zero in 2024.

instruments.explanation: Compulsory levies on the financial sector.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LV, D29H C03, C05 and C06

names.official: Land Register duties on transfers and pledges of property

taxes.base: Registering a change of ownership or a pledge in the Land Register, other than by inheritance or gift.
taxes.payer: Buyers and borrowers; legal and natural persons.

rate.headline: Set by the Law on Land Register Duties
details: EUR 22.4 million from natural persons and EUR 19.9 million from legal persons for the duty on ownership and pledge registration, plus EUR 2.2 million of stamp duties.

instruments.explanation: The nearest thing to a property transfer tax.

names.official: Duty on inheritances and gifts and the Land Register duties attached to them

taxes.base: Property received by inheritance or gift; the Land Register entries that record it.

rate.headline: Set by law
details: EUR 9.4 million from the duty itself, EUR 3.6 million from the connected Land Register duties in 2024.

instruments.explanation: The National Tax List calls these capital taxes.

names.official: Other state duties and fees

taxes.base: The small lines: the business risk duty (EUR 3.2 million), other special-purpose state duties (EUR 9.8 million), the foreigners’ payment for a residence permit (EUR 2.3 million), numbering rights (EUR 0.5 million), fishing licences and cards (EUR 1.4 million) and the duty for keeping animals (EUR 0.07 million).

instruments.explanation: Seven small lines of the National Tax List, together under 0.2% of the total.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LV, D29C, D29H C01, D29E C06 and C07, D59D, D91B

names.official: Personal income tax, share of the municipalities

taxes.base: The same tax as the State’s share: income of residents.

rate.headline: Same rates as the State’s share
details: Eurostat’s accounts record this part under local government (S.1313).

instruments.explanation: Most of the personal income tax goes to the municipalities, which makes it their main revenue. The rates are set by the Saeima and the State Revenue Service collects the tax.

names.official: Immovable property tax (land, buildings, engineering structures and dwellings)

taxes.base: The cadastral value of land, buildings and engineering structures; dwellings have their own line in the National Tax List.

rate.headline: Set within a range by the law and the municipality
details: EUR 193.9 million "tax on property" and EUR 43.4 million "immovable property tax on dwellings" in 2024 in the National Tax List.

instruments.explanation: The only broad tax that municipalities levy themselves.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LV, D29A C01 and C03
